description: #3830 — the two `property_definitions` WRITERS that answer with the row, driven through the command leg (`via: "command"`; neither appends an op, so the op log stays empty and `expected` carries only the seeded page). Pins `create_property_def`'s shape validation (bad value_type, bad key) and its INSERT OR IGNORE idempotency — a second create for the same key keeps the FIRST declaration, value_type and all — plus `update_property_def_options`' non-empty-JSON-array check, its select-type-only guard (the seeded text `note`) and its NotFound on an unknown key. Read back through the `list_property_defs` / `get_property_def` steps pinned by #4939. NOT pinned here: `conflicting_existing_values` (the #4399 probe that refuses a declaration which would orphan values the vault already holds under that key) — the mock has no equivalent, and the seed deliberately declares no `block_properties` row under either key. Re-author `expected` / `expected_ops` / `expected_queries` via CONFORMANCE_UPDATE=1.
name: property_def_writes

ops.comment: INSERT OR IGNORE idempotency: the existing row wins, so the response is still the SELECT definition with its options — not the text one this op asked for.
ops.name: create_existing_def_keeps_first

ops.comment: validate_property_def_shape refuses a value_type outside text/number/date/select/ref/boolean.
ops.name: create_def_bad_value_type_rejects

ops.comment: The happy path: the widened array is read back from inside the tx.

ops.comment: An empty array is refused before the row is touched, so priority_level keeps the three options above.

ops.name: update_options_on_text_def_rejects

ops.comment: An unknown key is NotFound, not a validation refusal.
ops.name: update_options_unknown_key_rejects

queries.comment: The point lookup the refusals above must have left alone.
